title: Restriction of the local identity-left proper/open seed
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $i:E\to F$ be a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathcal O_E)$ and $B=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathcal O_F)$, and use $D_H(Z)=D(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline H_Z)))$ and its normalized operations $J_H,R_H$ [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. Write $U_Z:D_B(Z)\to D_A(Z)$ for coefficient restriction and $o_j:U_ZJ_{A,j}\to J_{B,j}U_W$, $d_p:R_{B,p}U_T\to U_WR_{A,p}$ for openRestriction and properRestriction [def-pur-constant-scalar-tower-mates]. Write $P_Z^{(e)}$ for positive arithmetic selection of levels $e(n+1)$, $a_p:R_{B,p}P_T^{(e)}\to P_W^{(e)}R_{B,p}$ for reindexProper, and $b_j:J_{B,j}P_W^{(e)}\to P_Z^{(e)}J_{B,j}$ for reindexOpen [def-pur-strict-scalar-mate-evaluation-data]. Compositions of functors in these formulas are in execution order, as in Lean. Let $k:X\hookrightarrow W$ and $j:X\hookrightarrow T$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] that are quasi-compact (inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact), let $p:W\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and fix $h:kp=1_Xj$. Let
$$s_H=(\operatorname{rId}_H(X)^{-1}J_{H,j});\gamma_H(k,1_X,p,j,h):J_{H,j}\to J_{H,k}R_{H,p},$$
where the first factor is the inverse identity compositor whiskered by $J_{H,j}$ and $\gamma$ is the intrinsic clopen proper/open mate [def-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-arrows]. For every $N\in D_B(X)$,
$$s_A(U_XN);R_{A,p}(o_k(N));d_p^{-1}(J_{B,k}N)=o_j(N);U_T(s_B(N)).$$
For every $e\ge1$ and $N\in D_B(X)$,
$$P_T^{(e)}(s_B(N));a_p(J_{B,k}N);R_{B,p}(b_k(N))=b_j(N);s_B(P_X^{(e)}N).$$
Here semicolon denotes arrows followed from left to right. Neither assertion includes any subsequent proper image or proper-composition identification.

proof.text: Factor the identity-left proper/open square through its fibre product. Use the intrinsic clopen lift and its identity/zero projector. On ordinary modules coefficient restriction keeps both section components and the open-unit map, so the alpha comparison is unchanged. The same argument at every retained level applies to arithmetic selection, including all transitions.

Take the proper-adjunction mate with the ordered units and counits. Derive the ordinary section identities on whole strict diagrams, using the unitCompatible specification of properRestriction; finite-free tensor makes coefficient restriction preserve K-injectives. The identity-proper comparison is the specified rId, giving exactly the first seed equation.

For positive e use the exact left adjoint of arithmetic selection to preserve K-injectives. The ordinary identities are termwise, so their exact localization and the canonical derived-composite units give reindexOpen and reindexProper. Apply the same mate calculation, including the identity compositor, to obtain the second seed equation. No finite evaluation is used to detect equality.

lean.statement:
theorem strictRefinementSeedRestriction
    {X W T : Scheme.{u}} (k : X ⟶ W) (j : X ⟶ T) (p : W ⟶ T)
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact j]
    [IsProper p] (h : k ≫ p = (𝟙 X) ≫ j) :
    let A := ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)
    let B := ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l F)
    let sA := Functor.whiskerRight (rId A X).inv (J A j) ≫ gamma A k (𝟙 X) p j h
    let sB := Functor.whiskerRight (rId B X).inv (J B j) ≫ gamma B k (𝟙 X) p j h
    (∀ N : Derived B X,
      sA.app ((U l E F i X).obj N) ≫
          (R A p).map ((openRestriction l E F i k).hom.app N) ≫
          (properRestriction l E F i p).inv.app ((J B k).obj N) =
        (openRestriction l E F i j).hom.app N ≫ (U l E F i T).map (sB.app N)) ∧
    ∀ (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e) (N : Derived B X),
      (subsequence l F T e).map (sB.app N) ≫
          (reindexProper l F p e he).hom.app ((J B k).obj N) ≫
          (R B p).map ((reindexOpen l F k e).hom.app N) =
        (reindexOpen l F j e).hom.app N ≫ sB.app ((subsequence l F X e).obj N)
